# Feature Fields

Also called: Generalized NeRF, Semantic Fields

## Overview
Feature Fields generalize the standard Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) formulation by predicting arbitrary per-point feature signals $\mathbf{f}$ in addition to volume density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ [S1, unofficial]. This extension allows the 3D representation to encode semantic labels, physical properties, or latent embeddings from 2D foundation models, enabling tasks such as zero-shot segmentation and scene editing [S1, unofficial]. Unlike standard NeRF which only models appearance, this family lifts 2D observations into a consistent 3D representation by supervising the rendered features against 2D feature maps [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism modifies the radiance field function $F_\Theta$ to map input coordinates $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ to a tuple $(\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{c}, \sigma)$, where $\mathbf{f} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a feature vector [S1, unofficial]. The rendering of these features follows the same volume integration principle as color [G]. For a ray $r$, the rendered feature $\hat{\mathbf{F}}(r)$ is computed as:

$$
\hat{\mathbf{F}}(r) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{f}(x_i)
$$

where $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$ is the accumulated transmittance and $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$ is the opacity weight [G]. Supervision is performed by comparing the rendered feature $\hat{\mathbf{F}}(r)$ against ground-truth 2D feature maps or teacher network outputs projected onto the image plane [S1, unofficial]. This process lifts 2D observations into a consistent 3D representation [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Multi-Space Neural Radiance Field (MS-NeRF)](11707-multi-space-neural-radiance-field-ms-nerf.md)
Represents the scene using a group of feature fields in parallel sub-spaces instead of a single radiance field. It sets itself apart by automatically handling mirror-like objects without manual labeling, unlike single-space NeRF which often requires it. Choose this method for scenes with reflective and refractive objects where standard NeRF fails to maintain multi-view consistency.

### [NRFF](12072-nrff.md)
Encodes view-dependent effects, specifically specularities, using a multiscale tensor decomposition and Anisotropic Spherical Gaussians (ASG). It differs from siblings by explicitly modeling reflection geometry in a latent space via a Rendering Equation Encoding (REE) before the directional MLP, avoiding explicit roughness maps. Choose this for scenes requiring accurate specular highlight modeling.

### [Semantic and Feature Branches](12095-semantic-and-feature-branches.md)
Extends the standard NeRF formulation by predicting arbitrary per-point feature signals $\mathbf{f}$ in addition to color and density. It provides the general mechanism for lifting 2D feature observations into a consistent 3D representation, unlike siblings focused on specific downstream applications. Choose this for zero-shot segmentation, object manipulation, or 3D detection requiring general feature fields.

### [NeRF for Object Segmentation](12404-nerf-for-object-segmentation.md)
Extends NeRF to perform object segmentation by simultaneously estimating scene geometry and predicting semantic occlusion masks. It introduces "area encoding" to represent occlusion probability, specifically targeting binary or probabilistic masks for 3D de-occlusion and inpainting. Choose this when 3D de-occlusion and inpainting are required.

### [Semantic-NeRF](14889-semantic-nerf.md)
Synthesizes semantic labels for novel views by predicting a semantic feature vector alongside color and density. It sets itself apart by focusing on the direct integration of categorical semantic labels via a dedicated output branch, rather than general feature fields or instance-specific segmentation. Choose this for multi-view consistent semantic understanding and label propagation from sparse or noisy annotations.

### [Augmented Features (Avg, Var, Color)](15000-augmented-features-avg-var-color.md)
Enhances volumetric scene representation by enriching the feature space with statistical moments (mean, variance) and low-level appearance cues. It sets itself apart by focusing on statistical geometry priors (variance) for multi-view 3D object detection, rather than semantic labels. Choose this for multi-view 3D object detection where geometric priors are insufficient.

### Object Field Representation
A function $f(\mathbf{p})$ that maps a 3D point $\mathbf{p}$ to an object code vector $\mathbf{o}$, representing object ownership independent of viewing angles [S2, unofficial]. The object code $\mathbf{o}$ is defined as $H+1$ dimensional, where $H$ is a predefined maximum number of solid objects the network predicts, and the last dimension represents empty space to handle occlusion and collision [S2, unofficial]. The function $f$ is parameterized by a series of MLPs [S2, unofficial].

### N3F
A method that learns additional feature fields to realize self-supervised 3D segmentation [S3].

### NeRF Branch Feature Sampling and Augmentation
Augments sampled features with variance from multiple views to describe occupancy: low variance implies occupied 3D location (Lambertian assumption), while high variance implies free space (different appearances from different views) [S4]. Points are sampled along the ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t \times \mathbf{d}$ [S4]. Augmented features are computed by sampling from high-resolution 2D image features (typically $160 \times 120$) instead of low-resolution volume features ($40 \times 40 \times 16$) to address aliasing [S4]. The augmented feature $\bar{V}$ is a concatenation of $\{V_{avg}, V_{var}, \text{RGB}_{avg}, \text{RGB}_{var}\}$ [S4]. Density and latent features are computed as $\sigma(\mathbf{p}), \hat{\mathbf{h}}(\mathbf{p}) = \text{G-MLP}(\bar{V}(\mathbf{p}), \gamma(\mathbf{p}))$, and color as $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{p}, \mathbf{d}) = \text{C-MLP}(\hat{\mathbf{h}}(\mathbf{p}), \mathbf{d})$ [S4]. Sampling from image features achieves 20.51 PSNR for novel-view synthesis compared to 18.93 with volume sampling [S4].

### Feature Sampling from Multi-View 2D Features
Samples point features along the ray from multi-view image features instead of low-resolution volume features to address the need for high-resolution images in NeRF [S4]. This approach achieves 20.51 PSNR for novel-view synthesis compared to 18.93 with volume sampling [S4].

## Background
The concept of feature fields generalizes the NeRF formulation, which originally maps $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\mathbf{c}, \sigma)$, to predict arbitrary per-point feature signals $\mathbf{f}$ [S1, unofficial]. Semantic-NeRF was the first to introduce semantic fields within the NeRF framework, using ground-truth semantic segmentation maps to augment the radiance field with per-point semantic logits [S1, unofficial]. Subsequent works have extended this to include physical properties, latent descriptors from 2D foundation models, and object codes [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial][S3].
